title: Wind Moves a Ball on the Putting Green
question: Hannah’s ball lies on the putting green and has not been marked or lifted. A gust of wind moves the ball to a new position. What should Hannah do?

choices.text: Replace the ball on its original spot.
Play the ball from its new position.
Replace the ball and take a one-stroke penalty.

explanation: When a ball at rest is moved by natural forces such as wind or water, Rule 9.3 states the player must play the ball from its new position. There is no penalty and the ball is not replaced unless it was already lifted and replaced.
imagePrompt: A polished, modern, semi-realistic golf illustration (roughly 75% realistic, 25% stylised) of a junior golfer standing on a putting green on a windy day. Show her watching as her golf ball, which has not been marked or lifted, has been moved by the wind to a new position on the green. The original ball position should be just visible as a faint mark or impression. The grass and flag in the background should show visible wind movement, such as blowing leaves or a flapping flag. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: Junior golfer on a windy putting green watching her ball after it has been moved by the wind, with the original spot faintly visible.

sceneSpec.setting: A putting green on a golf course, on a windy day.
sceneSpec.players: One junior golfer, Hannah, is standing and watching her ball on the green.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Her original ball position on the green is visible, and the ball has just finished rolling to a new position on the green after being moved by a gust of wind.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment immediately after a gust of wind has moved the ball on the putting green.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Demonstrates what must be done when natural forces move a ball on the putting green before it is marked or lifted.
mustShow: A junior golfer observing her golf ball on the putting green.
The ball at rest in its new position, with a faint impression or divot showing where it originally lay.
